reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Clear evidence of target engagement with CD4+ T cell responses observed across arms, ranging from 0 participants (arm A) to 15 participants (arm D). The vaccine successfully engaged its intended target of Class II MHC-restricted helper peptides to stimulate CD4+ responses. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Mixed evidence of downstream biology changes. While CD4+ T cell responses were generated (especially in arm D), tumor infiltration data shows concerning patterns - both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in tumor tissue decreased from baseline to day 22 (CD8: 401→293, CD4: 1202→1102 cells/mm2), suggesting the systemic immune activation may not have translated to enhanced tumor infiltration. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: This was a Phase I safety/immunogenicity study, so clinical efficacy endpoints were not the primary focus. The primary endpoint was safety and immunogenicity, with variable success across arms. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Clear dose-response relationship across adjuvant combinations - arm D (6MHP + polyICLC + Montanide + cyclophosphamide) showed the strongest CD4+ response (15 participants), while simpler combinations showed progressively weaker responses. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This is a dose-escalation/combination-finding study with small sample size (48 total) and short duration (12.1 weeks). The sepsis event in the cyclophosphamide arm represents a safety concern but didn't prevent dosing.

failure_modes.evidence: Clear differential response across arms - arm D with full adjuvant combination showed strong CD4+ response (15 participants) while simpler combinations showed progressively weaker responses (arm A: 0, arm B: 2, arm C: 4 participants)
